description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve revenue management, and local service delivery nationwide and in the education sector in Selected Regions.

The development objective of the Public Sector Performance Project for Madagascar is to improve revenue management, and local service delivery nationwide and in the education sector in selected regions. The project comprises of four components. The first component, improving revenue management seeks to address a number of functional problems that limit the efficiency of revenue generation and collection in key revenues agencies (tax, customs, and mining). The second component, improving service delivery capacity of local governments seeks to address a number of functional problems that undermine service delivery and resilience at the local level. The third component, improving governance mechanisms in the education sector seeks to address a number of functional problems that affect budget execution and service delivery at the local level and in the education sector. The fourth component, improving controls and performance monitoring seeks to address a number of functional problems that undermine the efficient use of scarce resources.

title.narrative: C1-3. Number of revenue offices that have been subject to external evaluation of their performance contracts/program

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was not met. While 39 performance contracts were signed for both the tax and customs office, the Court of Account could not undertake their external evaluation. which was a prerequisite for this indicator's achievement</p>

title.narrative: C1-5. Establishment of a single administrative identification number

target.value: Publication of quarterly data matching analysis between customs, tax and pension fund

comment.narrative: <p>The structure of the Unique Identity Number for legal entities that was a prerequisite for data matching and data analysis was approved by the Government in 2021 but pending formal adoption through a decree. By the time the project closed,  no publication on matching data analysis between customs, taxes and the pension fund was undertaken. However, under the PRODIGY project, an interoperability platform was set-up and the three entities have started working on data matching. </p>

title.narrative: C4-2. High/substantial risks audits completed by Internal Audit Departments

comment.narrative: <p>Three high risks audit were undertaken in 2021. These high risks audits were namely : audit report on currency declaration at borders, audit on ineligible expenditures of the CASEF project (Bank funded project), audit on ineligible expenditures of the PRODUIR project (Bank funded project)</p>

title.narrative: C3.1 - Share of schools targeted by the component with an operational FEFFI, planning and implementing PECs

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was exceeded the expected end target of 65% </p>

title.narrative: C4-3. Semiannual public debates on the budget law, the performance of revenue agencies and project performance led by CSOs.

comment.narrative: <p>CSO hold 2 debates on budget and 1 debate on Public Investment </p>

title.narrative: PDO 1- Increased tax revenue collection (Domestic tax revenue/GDP ratio)

comment.narrative:
<p>The end target is not achieved. New targets were set as part of the second restructuring following the GDP rebasing done in 2019to align with the latest population general census. This indicator was particularly affected by COVID-19 crisis. To mitigate the issue and increase performance, the tax administration has started adopting digital solution with the objective to deploy a comprehensive Integrated Fiscal Administration System. </p>
<p> </p>

<p>This indicator received considerable traction from the Tax Administration but the different strategies to improve and acceleratetax payers enrollment and business formalization were significantly slowed down by the health emergency situation with episodes of government shut downs and subnational borders closed. </p>

title.narrative: C2-2. Improved recovery of revenue (not including grants) by local governments

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was not met. Revenue collection at subnational level was particularly affected by the heath emergency situation and quality and on the ground support could not be provided. </p>

title.narrative: C1-2. Increased rate of confirmed suspicious customs transactions related to home use in selected Custom Office (in case of physical examination).

comment.narrative: <p>The end target was not met although some progress was recorded between January and June 2021. Concerned ports included : Toamasina, Ivato, Fort Dauphin, Majunga andTuléar</p>

title.narrative: C3-2. Percentage of FRAM teachers in the areas selected by the component receiving subsidies with less than two months of delay

comment.narrative:
<p>Due to school closure during the Covid-19 pandemic, FRAM teachers were not paid during part of 2020-2021 school year</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: PDO 2 - Number of TADAT PO-8 indicators "Efficient Revenue Management" rated B (Text, Custom)

comment.narrative: <p>In December 2021, a second round of TADAT training was conducted with extended participants from audit institution, private sector and civil society. The actual target achieved at completion was defined following a TADAT self-evaluation exercise undertaken as part of the trainings and with support and guidance from IMF and AFRITAC SUD.  This self evaluation concluded that only one indicator in the Performance Outcome Area 8 (Efficient Revenue Management) was rated B (P8-26 : Contribution to government tax revenue forecasting process). An external evaluation is scheduled in the first quarter of 2022 to capture initial effect of the ITAS in improving fiscal management in the country.</p>

title.narrative: C2-1. Improved timeliness of service-delivery fiscal transfers to local governments

baseline.value: No standard available to measure acceptable delays for transfer execution

target.value: Completion of transfers of all investment and operating subventions to communes by July 2021

comment.narrative:
<p>This indicator was considered achieved by the Court of Account in its final verification report. While all operating grants transfers were fully transferred by the end of July, investment grants transfers registered a 60 days average delay to be fully processed due to lengthy procedures and necessary adjustments at the MEF level. Because this indicator was a timebound PBC, it could not be considered for disbursement as per the financing agreement. Nonetheless, the Government has gradually increased the amount of both grants throughout the project timeline and had cleared all previous arrears by the project's closing </p>
<p> </p>

actual.value: Transfers completed but with an average delay of 60 days

title.narrative: C1-1. Modernization of the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS)

target.value: Publication of external ITAS performance Audit report.

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was not met. The audit was not completed by the time the Court of Account published its verification report (December 15, 2021). Since the PRODIGY project is taking over the ITAS development, it was agreed that this audit will be undertaken as part of ITAS development under PRODIGY. </p>

title.narrative: C4-1. Timely availability of the Court of Acccount (CA) public report (process indicator)

target.value: Yes, 8 months after the end of considered FY

comment.narrative: <p>The Court of Account has consistently published its annual report before the end of a given year and publicly presented the report at national and subnational level</p>

actual.value: Less than 12 months after the end of considered FY

title.narrative: PDO 5 - Number of female beneficiaries participating into public debates

comment.narrative: <p>This PDO indicator exceeded its end target. During the second restructuring, the indicator on the number of women direct beneficiaries was replaced by the number of women participating into public debates as the former was challenging to accurately measure given the national scope of the project. This revision was made to have a more manageable to collect and measure indicator. Public debates are organized both at national and subnational level by CSOs.</p>

title.narrative: PDO 3 - Share of communes undertaking an IGL self-assessment published on government public service delivery performance website

baseline.value: IGL self assessment tool not available

target.value: 400 communes undertake their IGL self assessment and publish it

comment.narrative: <p>This PDO was achieved. In December 2021, the government published the score of 450 communes which undertook their IGL self-evaluation. Results are available on https://mid.gov.mg/oddl-igl</p>

actual.value: 450 communes undertook their IGL assessment and published it

title.narrative: PDO 4 - Publication of a Human resource management report within the Ministry of Education

target.value: Online publication of HRM dashboard by school and by teacher on a quarterly basis within 15 days of the start of each quarter

comment.narrative: <p>At the project's closing, the dashboard was published but not updated on an quarterly basis. Therefore, this indicator is only partially achieved </p>

actual.value: Education's HRM dashboard publicly available online

title.narrative: C1-6. Improved formal registration of small and individual businesses

comment.narrative: <p>Thanks to a joint effort with the Economic Development Board of Madagascar, the project was able to secure this indicator since the first semester of 2021.</p>
